title: The beach, again
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Every morning now: the beach. The strip draws the same walk it drew two weeks ago and it's different. The dog knows the way. Wood doesn't lead; he follows a sock.

panels.composition: The beach at dawn, gray, the tide out. BARNABY ahead, the sock in his mouth. WOOD behind.

image.prompt: a gray Pacific Northwest beach at dawn with a small dog trotting ahead carrying a sock and a young man following, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog stopping at a log. Wood stopping. The dog looking back: this one.

image.prompt: a small dog stopped at a driftwood log on a beach, looking back at a young man, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The log. A drawing on it? No. Barnacles. But Wood looks.

image.prompt: close on a barnacled driftwood log on a beach, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The two of them past the log, on toward the spruce grove. The strip has a route now and didn't choose it.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog walking a gray beach toward a dark spruce grove at its edge, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The route is the dog's. The log appears; the walk map (2007) begins here without knowing.
